Symbol Dictionary

¶5. What Salvation Really Is — Saved From Sin

Section 5 of 10 · ≈15 min

In This Section

The angel named the Saviour by His work — "he shall save his people FROM their sins" — from sin's guilt, from sin's dominion, and at last from sin's very presence, by the indwelling Christ restoring the image of God in the soul; a gospel that leaves men under sin's rule until death is not the everlasting gospel.

The Saviour is named by His work — Matt. 1:21, 23; Ps. 130:8:

  • Matt. 1:21. "thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins" — the name is the work: He saves His people FROM their sins — not from the penalty only, and never leaving them IN them; Jesus (Heb. Yeshua) = "Jehovah saves," and what Jehovah saves from is the sin itself.
    • salvation = God saving man FROM sin — from its guilt (justification, the pardon of Matt. 1:21), from its power and dominion (sanctification, Rom. 6:14, 18, 22; John 8:36), and at last from its very presence (glorification, 1 John 3:2); the restoration of the image of God in the soul (Col. 3:10; 2 Cor. 3:18), effected by the indwelling Christ (Col. 1:27; Gal. 2:20), reaching "to the uttermost" (Heb. 7:25) — not a legal status only but a Person possessed and a nature renewed.
  • Matt. 1:23. "they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us" — the paired name gives the method: He saves from sin by being God WITH us — and, the mystery carried to its end, God IN us (Col. 1:27); the Person present is the power that saves.
  • Ps. 130:8. "And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities" — the Old Testament promise Matthew 1:21 fulfils: redemption FROM all iniquities, not toleration of them; "all" leaves no reserved sin under which the redeemed remain.
  • WitnessEVCO 18.1. Waggoner: "It is a message of salvation from sin" — the everlasting gospel named in one sentence, grounded on the angel's word to Joseph in Matthew 1:21.

What sin is, He treats as bondage — and breaks it — John 8:34-36:

  • John 8:34. "Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin" — Christ's diagnosis: sin is not a debt only but a slavery; the consented transgression (see “What Sin Is — Transgression, Not Inheritance”) makes the sinner a slave.
  • John 8:35. "the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the Son abideth ever" — the slave has no standing in the house; only the Son can confer a sonship that abides.
  • John 8:36. "If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed" — the freedom He gives is not nominal; "indeed" — it actually severs the slavery.
  • WitnessDA 466.3. White: "Christ came to break the shackles of sin-slavery from the soul" — quoting John 8:36 itself; the soul that refuses to give himself to God "may talk of freedom, but he is in the most abject slavery" — the pardon that leaves the chains on is not the freedom Christ gives.

Made free from sin — guilt and dominion dealt with together — Rom. 6:6, 14, 18, 22:

  • Rom. 6:6. our old man is crucified with Him, "that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin" — the cross's stated purpose in the believer: not forgiven continuance in sin, but the end of sin's service.
  • Rom. 6:14. "For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace" — this is grace's own definition: deliverance from sin's DOMINION; a gospel that leaves men under sin's rule contradicts the very clause that defines being "under grace" (walked in full in "Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame").
  • Rom. 6:18. "Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness" — the section's term verbatim, in the present tense: freedom from sin is a stated fact for the believer, issuing at once in a new servitude — to righteousness.
  • Rom. 6:22. "But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life" — the whole arc in one verse: freedom now, holiness as fruit, everlasting life at the end.
  • WitnessWOR 71.1. Waggoner: the blessedness of the man to whom God imputes righteousness is "the blessedness of sins forgiven, and of freedom from the power of sin" — pardon and power are one blessedness, never separated in the gospel.
  • WitnessLOF_ATJ 147.4. Jones, on Rom. 6:18: "Being then made free from sin, YE BECAME THE SERVANTS OF RIGHTEOUSNESS.... He says you are, and when He says you are, it is so.... He has made you so, for He says so" — the deliverance is received on God's word, as fact.
  • WitnessLOF_ATJ 85.2. Jones: the power of God is given for "deliverance from sin and from the power of it, the reign of righteousness in the life" — and he rebukes the truncated gospel: "Many believe and receive the grace of God for the salvation from sins that are past but are content with that and do not give it the same place in the soul to reign against the power of sin."
  • WitnessGTI 190.2. Waggoner: coming to Jesus, the Mediator of the new covenant, "we become free from sin,—from transgression of the law" — with "grace to help us in the hour of temptation" and "cleansing from all sin"; the freedom reaches the very hour of the trial.

The righteousness of the law fulfilled IN us — God works the obedience — Rom. 8:3-4; Eze. 36:25-27:

  • Rom. 8:3. "God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh" — in the very flesh He took (see “The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took”), sin was condemned — dethroned in its own stronghold.
  • Rom. 8:4. "That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit" — the purpose clause of the incarnation: not imputed righteousness only, but the law's righteousness wrought IN the believer by the Spirit.
  • WitnessGTI 199.1. Waggoner: "And why does He make us free from sin?—In order that we may live free from sin" — Christ, who has power over all flesh, strengthens us by His Spirit "that the righteousness of the law may be fulfilled in us."
  • Eze. 36:25. "Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you" — the covenant promise beneath the whole New Testament: cleansing from ALL filthiness, defilement removed, not managed.
  • Eze. 36:26-27. "A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you... I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes" — God Himself works the walking; salvation from sin's power is a divine operation, not a human resolve — the new-birth promise in covenant form (see “Born of Water and of the Spirit — How He Lived, How We Begin”).

The power of it is not a status but a Person — Col. 1:27; Gal. 2:20:

  • Col. 1:27. "which is Christ in you, the hope of glory" — the mystery of the gospel is not a ledger entry only but a Person possessed; the indwelling Saviour is Himself the pledge that the work will be finished.
  • Gal. 2:20. "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God" — the mechanism of salvation from sin's power: the old self crucified, and an indwelling Life living the new life "in the flesh" by faith — not the man's effort, but Christ's own living.
  • WitnessCT 194.1. White: "When Christ is formed within, the hope of glory, then the truth of God will so act upon the natural temperament that its transforming power will be seen in changed characters" — the authority of God over the man "not in name only, but in reality and truth."
  • WitnessEVCO 23.2. Waggoner: "the power by which Christ saves men from sin is the power by which He created the worlds" — the everlasting gospel preaches Christ "the creative power of God"; salvation from sin is a Creator's act, a re-creation, not a reform.

What is being restored: the image of God — Col. 3:9-10; 2 Cor. 3:18:

  • Col. 3:9. "seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds" — the old man is put OFF, deeds and all; salvation does not whitewash him, it removes him.
  • Col. 3:10. "put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him" — the new man is renewed after the Creator's own image: salvation reverses the fall by re-creating in the soul the likeness that sin marred.
  • 2 Cor. 3:18. "beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory" — the process named: progressive transformation into Christ's image by beholding Him, wrought "as by the Spirit of the Lord" — Colossians 3:10 in motion.
  • WitnessDA 37.3. White: "Jesus came to restore in man the image of his Maker. None but Christ can fashion anew the character that has been ruined by sin" — He came "to reshape the marred character after the pattern of His divine character."
  • WitnessEd 125.2. White: the central theme of the whole Bible is "the redemption plan, the restoration in the human soul of the image of God" — salvation from sin IS image-restoration; the two are one definition.

To the uttermost — sins taken away, the devil's works destroyed — Heb. 7:25; 1 John 3:5, 8; Titus 2:14:

  • Heb. 7:25. "he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them" — the section's term verbatim: to the UTTERMOST — completely, to the last extremity of sin's hold; His unbroken priestly life guarantees a salvation that reaches all the way, not a partial rescue.
  • 1 John 3:5. "he was manifested to take away our sins; and in him is no sin" — removal, not mere covering; the sinless One was manifested for the express purpose of taking sin AWAY.
  • 1 John 3:8. "For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil" — sin is the devil's work; a salvation that leaves that work intact in the saved fails the very purpose for which the Son was manifested.
  • Titus 2:14. "that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works" — Christ's self-gift has twin objects: redemption from all iniquity and purification of a people; guilt and defilement dealt with together.
  • WitnessPCP 48.2. White: "He takes away our sins, and makes us partakers of His holiness.... He is able to save unto the uttermost all who come unto God by Him" — removal of sin joined to impartation of holiness; the two halves of the uttermost salvation.

And at last, from sin's presence — a people without spot — 1 John 3:2-3; Eph. 5:25-27:

  • 1 John 3:2. "now are we the sons of God... when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is" — glorification: the last stage of salvation, deliverance from sin's very PRESENCE at His appearing.
  • 1 John 3:3. "And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure" — the future likeness works backward: the hope of being like Him purifies NOW, "even as he is pure."
  • Eph. 5:25-26. "Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word" — the present tense of His love: sanctifying and cleansing now.
  • Eph. 5:27. "That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish" — the end of the everlasting gospel: a people actually cleansed from sin, not merely accounted so — the church He presents at last (ripened in "The Harvest — A People in Whom Christ Is Vindicated").

Synthesis

DEFINITION — WHAT SALVATION REALLY IS — SAVED FROM SIN = salvation is God saving His people FROM their sins (Matt. 1:21; Ps. 130:8) — from sin's guilt in justification, the pardon of Matt. 1:21 ("the blessedness of sins forgiven," WOR 71.1), from sin's power and dominion in sanctification ("being then made free from sin," Rom. 6:14, 18, 22; "free indeed," John 8:36), and at last from sin's very presence in glorification ("we shall be like him," 1 John 3:2; "not having spot, or wrinkle," Eph. 5:27). It is the restoration of the image of God in the soul (Col. 3:9-10; 2 Cor. 3:18; DA 37.3; Ed 125.2), and its power is not a legal status only but a Person possessed — "Christ in you, the hope of glory" (Col. 1:27), the crucified-with-Christ life in which "Christ liveth in me" (Gal. 2:20) — the same creative power that made the worlds (EVCO 23.2) now working in the believer what God promised in the covenant: "I will... cause you to walk in my statutes" (Eze. 36:25-27; Rom. 8:3-4). Christ was manifested "to take away our sins" and "destroy the works of the devil" (1 John 3:5, 8), and He "is able also to save them to the uttermost" (Heb. 7:25) — therefore, as the message that came to the fore at Minneapolis in 1888 and was preached in the years following pressed home (LOF_ATJ 85.2; GTI 199.1), a gospel that receives grace only for "sins that are past" while leaving sin's power enthroned, a gospel that leaves men under sin's dominion until death, is not the everlasting gospel; it is salvation IN sin, and the angel's word forbids it: He saves His people FROM their sins.

Symbols Defined Here

  • salvation = God saving man FROM sin — from its guilt (justification), from its power and dominion (sanctification), and at last from its very presence (glorification); the restoration of the image of God in the soul by the indwelling Christ — not a legal status only but a Person possessed and a nature renewed — reaching to the uttermost (Matt. 1:21; Ps. 130:8; Rom. 6:18, 22; John 8:36; Col. 3:10; 2 Cor. 3:18; Col. 1:27; Gal. 2:20; Heb. 7:25; 1 John 3:2-3, 5, 8; Titus 2:14).

Symbols Carried

sin = the consented transgression of the law, the slavery here broken (see “What Sin Is — Transgression, Not Inheritance”); the likeness of sinful flesh in which sin was condemned = the nature Christ took (see “The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took”); the new heart and the washing = the new birth by water and the Spirit (see “Born of Water and of the Spirit — How He Lived, How We Begin”); the faith by which Christ lives in the believer is walked in full in "Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel’s Message in Verity," and the dominion broken here is proved complete in "Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame."

For Discussion

  1. Matt. 1:21 says He saves His people "from their sins," and Jones warns of those who "receive the grace of God for the salvation from sins that are past but are content with that." Where in your own life have you quietly settled for pardon without deliverance — and what would it mean this week to claim Rom. 6:14 as a promise rather than an ideal?
  2. Rom. 6:14 makes freedom from sin's dominion the very definition of being "under grace." Is there a "reserved sin" you have quietly accepted as permanent — and what does "I will... cause you to walk in my statutes" (Eze. 36:27) promise about that very thing?
  3. Col. 1:27 and Gal. 2:20 make salvation a Person possessed, not a status only. In the next real temptation, what is the practical difference between trusting a changed record in heaven and trusting Christ living in you at that moment?
